KITCHEN LESSON · KITCHEN THINGS · AGES 3–6 YEARS

Cutting Board — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the cutting board as the chopping address: food ON the board, butter knife in hand, soft food first — real slicing, safely begun.

What is this?

A cutting board is the flat wooden stage where chopping happens — it holds the food still and keeps the counter (and the fingers) safe.

What does it mean?

The board card teaches a rule and a skill together: chopping happens on the board, never in the hand — and soft foods get the butter knife. This is the on-ramp to every knife skill to come.

What does the child need to know?

You need the board, a butter knife and a banana. The script: "the banana lives ON the board… the butter knife cuts… fingers on top, away from the blade." Coins for cereal, pride for the cook.

Why this matters

Real slicing jobs with safe tools are how young cooks earn their way toward bigger knives — years later, on a board just like this one. The path starts with a banana.

What it teaches

Two-hand coordination (hold and slice), the sawing motion, safe knife habits from day one, and snack independence — the sliced banana disappears.

Words to learn

cutting boardbutter knifeslicecoinssoftsteady

Say this to your child

“"Cutting board! The banana goes ON the board — never chop without it. Your butter knife… saw, saw… a banana coin! Again! Fingers on top of the banana, away from the blade. You are really slicing!"”

Step by step

  1. Stage the board: "cutting board! The chopping spot — food lives ON it."
  2. Butter knife briefing: "your knife — it cuts soft food. The sharp knives wait for big hands."
  3. The first slice: banana on the board, one hand steadying on TOP — "saw… saw… a coin!"
  4. The pile grows: coins for cereal, for pancakes, for eating straight off the board (quality control).
  5. The tidy: crumbs to the bin, board wiped, knife to the sink — the chef closes the kitchen.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "cutting board" sit over a wooden board with its handle hole — flat, worn and ready for its first banana.

Ask your child

"Where does chopping happen?" (on the board) "What does the butter knife cut?" (soft food) "Where do fingers go?" (on top, away from the blade)

What your child can say or do

Your child might slice every soft fruit in the house, serve banana coins at breakfast, or correct a visitor: "the board first!" — the rule, owned.

Out in the real world

Boards appear at every real knife moment: the chopping at the market stall, the carving at Christmas. "A cutting board — the chopping spot!" scales up with the cook.

Try it together

Snack Bar: a board, a butter knife, a bowl of soft fruit — the child runs the snack bar, slicing and serving. Payment accepted in bites and thank-yous.

Understanding check

Ask: "Where does food go for chopping?" (on the board) "What cuts the banana?" (the butter knife) "Where do fingers stay?" (on top, safe)

Staying safe

The board is where knife safety begins: chopping on the board, never in the hand; the butter knife for soft food only; the sharp knives are grown-ups’. Habits learned here are the ones that last.

This lesson pairs with the Cutting Board flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Kitchen Things.
